utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: This Status Conference is called to order. Madam Registrar, may you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-14-A, the Prosecutor versus Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask first, Mr. Blaskic, if you can hear the proceedings. Is there any problem with the translation? Can you hear me? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you well and I have no problem whatsoever with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I now call for the appearances. Let's start with Mr. Blaskic -- for the appellant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honour. Russell Hayman and Andrew Paley appearing on behalf of the appellant telephonically from Los Angeles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I know Mr. Paley is on the phone link.

utterances.speaker: MR. PALEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Anto Nobilo, also Defence counsel for General Blaskic, and I am here present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour. I'm Upawansa Yapa. I appear for the Prosecution with Mr. Norman Farrell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. The previous Status Conference was held on the 21st of February, and according to the Rules, particularly Rule 65 bis (B), a Status Conference has to be called at least every 120 days. The purpose of this Status Conference is, on the one hand, to update the appellant with respect to the state of his appeal, and on the other hand, to allow the appellant to express any concerns as to his detention conditions, and directly through counsel, of course. Now, let me first perhaps ask Mr. Blaskic and his counsel if they have any concern to address concerning the conditions of detention. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no questions to raise regarding my treatment in the Detention Unit of the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Blaskic, and I remind you that in case any problem arises, you may avail yourself of the Rules concerning complaints, if the case may be. Now, as to the appeal, the situation is at the moment the following: In April, on the 19th of April, the Prosecution submitted its response to the appellant's brief in support of his motion to admit additional evidence on appeal, according to Rule 115 of the Rules. And the deadline for the appellant to file his reply brief in support of this motion expires on the 18th of June, 2001. That is exactly today. I haven't received anything, but perhaps in between this reply has been filed, although it hasn't reached my desk. So if, as I understand, the reply has been submitted today, the Appeal Chamber will have to decide on the admission -- on the motion on the admission of the additional evidence. I just had confirmation that the reply has been filed today. So as I say, the Appeal Chamber will have to make a decision on the motion. What I can probably say, that this decision will require some time because the parties -- there's a large volume of documentary evidence that has been tendered and the Appeal Chamber will have to carefully review all this documentary evidence, and I can foresee that that will require some time. But of course, the parties will be informed in due course when the Appeal Chamber will make a decision on the evidence, on the additional evidence. And once that will be done, we will resume a Briefing Schedule, but I can think that won't be before, let's say, a couple of months at least. But then we have summer, so it will be after summer, probably. Will be in September or so. This is the situation as I see it, as I see it now. Are there any matters to be raised as far as this motion is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I understand it's not the case. So may I ask the parties if there is any other matter that they want to raise at this stage in the Status Conference. The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: No, we do not have any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: No. Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so, unless my colleague, Russell Hayman, who is now on the telephone, has something to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, I heard your colleague on the phone saying at the same time that he had nothing to raise. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. We look forward to further communication from the Appellant Chamber concerning our motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. So if there are no other matters to be dealt with, I think we can adjourn the meeting, so the meeting stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
